topic: How does the human heart pump blood?

claims.claim: The heart has four chambers: two upper chambers (atria) and two lower chambers (ventricles).
Oxygen-poor blood from the body enters the right atrium; the right ventricle pumps it to the lungs.
Oxygen-rich blood from the lungs enters the left atrium, passes to the left ventricle, and the left ventricle pumps it to the whole body.
The heart has four valves (tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, aortic); they prevent blood from flowing backward.
The heartbeat sounds ('lub-dub') are made by heart valves closing ('lub': valves between atria and ventricles; 'dub': aortic and pulmonary valves).
Each heartbeat begins with an electrical signal from pacemaker cells in the sinoatrial (SA) node in the right atrium.
A resting heart rate of 60 to 100 beats per minute is normal for adults.
claims.note: the script says 'at rest ... 60 to 100 times a minute'

claims.claim: The left ventricle generates the high pressure needed to pump blood to the whole body.
